== Basics ==
'''Intelligence or Wisdom, whichever is higher governs your chance to gain skill increases.'''

Jewelry Making, commonly referred to as jewelcrafting or simply JC, allows you to make various rings, earrings, bracelets and veils. Some of these creations are popular and over the long run jewelcrafting can be a good source of income. However, Jewelry Making can be very expensive to skill up: getting to skill level 162 (needed for the {{:Runed Coldain Prayer Shawl}}) can cost upwards of three thousand platinum pieces (Gnome Necro with 228 INT, 56 CHA took about 2,500 plat to hit 162 skill - Halfling Druid, 250 WIS, 61 CHA took 1,410 plat to hit 162, higher wis/int seems to make a big difference in skill up frequency). While unenchanted jewelry combines do produce skillups, only enchanted versions have any bonus statistics. NPCs also pay slightly more for an enchanted version of the same item. Jewelry Making is an ideal tradeskill for [[Enchanter|Enchanters]] because they are the only class that can enchant metal bars. You'll need a [[Jeweler's Kit]] to combine the pieces in.

When calculating the [[TradeskillTable|success rates]] vs. the cost of creating items with more expensive gems it becomes clear that sometimes it is cheaper to skip ahead. For instance, at trivial 46 the cost of a [[Silvered Peridot Ring]] is over ~10p with a success rate of 64%. While at trivial 74 the cost of a [[Electrum Malachite Bracelet]] is only ~2.6p at a success rate of 40%. So, skipping to the [[Electrum Malachite Bracelet]] ends up being cheaper. A similar point is around skill 114, the [[Electrum Peridot Bracelet]]. Mileage may vary depending on your characters stats.

Note: [[Solusek Ro | Solusek Ro's]] Jewelry not only has a deity restriction but a class restriction, only usable by [[Bard]]s and [[Wizard]]s.
